title: Signature Lantern Clock Mark I
body:
Specifications: The Signature Lantern Clock Mark I is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. It follows the lantern form: four brass pillars, pierced frets, and a finial, but its movement is laid out for modern servicing with all pivots reachable from the back.

Mechanism: A weight-driven verge and foliot movement regulates the Mark I, with a countwheel strike on a bell. The foliot weights slide on a graduated bar, so the beat can be set by scale rather than by trial alone.

Maintenance: Wind the Mark I daily, keep it level, and dust the frets with a soft brush. Set the foliot weights equally, using the graduated scale as a guide.

Build and restoration: The back plate removes on four screws for servicing. Tools: screwdrivers, soft brush, oil, tweezers, and a timing chart.

title: Signature Foliot Lantern Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Foliot Lantern Clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its foliot is a balanced bar with brass weights that screw along threaded ends, giving fine regulation without moving weights by hand.

Mechanism: The verge and foliot regulate a weight-driven going train, and a countwheel strike sounds the hour on a bell. The threaded foliot weights move in small, repeatable steps, so the rate can be set and recorded.

Maintenance: Regulate by turning both weights equally, one turn at a time, and timing the clock over a full day. Keep the crown wheel and pallets clean and lightly oiled.

Build and restoration: The foliot weights are turned with a small key supplied with the clock. Tools: setting key, oil, tweezers, magnification, and a timing chart.

title: Signature Twin-Weight Lantern Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Twin-Weight Lantern Clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. It uses two matched going weights instead of one, so the going train is driven evenly from both sides of the barrel.

Mechanism: The two weights hang on twin lines wound on a double barrel, and their combined fall drives the going train through a single great wheel. The strike train has its own weight as usual, so the clock uses three weights in total.

Maintenance: Wind all three weights on schedule and check that the twin lines wind evenly, without overlapping. If one line winds faster, the barrel needs re-levelling.

Build and restoration: The double barrel is reached from the movement back. Tools: gut line, screwdrivers, oil, tweezers, and a weight scale.

title: Signature Single-Hand Lantern Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Single-Hand Lantern Clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its dial is a single-hand chapter ring with bold Roman numerals and quarter marks, made for reading the hour at a distance.

Mechanism: The hour hand is driven from the hour wheel arbor, and the movement is a weight-driven verge and foliot design with a countwheel strike. The bold numerals are engraved, not printed, so they survive cleaning.

Maintenance: Read the clock by the hour numeral and the quarter marks, and set it by moving the hand to the correct hour. Wind daily and keep the clock level.

Build and restoration: The dial lifts off for cleaning with a soft dry brush. Tools: soft brush, screwdrivers, oil, and a dial template.

title: Signature Bell-Tower Lantern Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Bell-Tower Lantern Clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its top carries a small open bell tower with two bells, one for the hour and one for the quarters, instead of a single bell.

Mechanism: The strike train sounds the hour on the larger bell, and a quarter train sounds a single blow on the smaller bell at each quarter hour. The going train is a weight-driven verge and foliot movement.

Maintenance: Keep both bells dust-free and check that each hammer falls squarely. Wind on schedule and keep the clock level.

Build and restoration: The bells are mounted on a removable bar for cleaning. Tools: hammer-setting gauge, screwdrivers, oil, and a pitch reference.

title: Signature Alarm Lantern Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Alarm Lantern Clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its alarm disc is set from the dial front with a knob, rather than from behind, so the alarm hour can be set without removing the clock from its bracket.

Mechanism: The alarm disc carries a notch that releases the alarm train when the hour hand reaches it, ringing a second bell until stopped. The going and strike trains are standard weight-driven lantern trains.

Maintenance: Set the alarm knob in the evening and test it once by hand. If the alarm fails, the disc notch or release lever needs cleaning.

Build and restoration: The alarm disc is reached from the dial front. Tools: screwdrivers, tweezers, oil, and an alarm test chart.

title: Signature Converted-Pendulum Lantern Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Converted-Pendulum Lantern Clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. It is designed as a pendulum clock from the start, with a long pendulum hanging below the lantern frame, rather than as a converted foliot clock.

Mechanism: A verge escapement with a crutch drives a 1 metre pendulum, giving a two-second period and accuracy of a few minutes a week. The countwheel strike sounds the hour on a bell.

Maintenance: Hang the clock so the pendulum swings freely below it, clear of the bracket and wall. Wind on schedule and keep the suspension spring undamaged.

Build and restoration: The pendulum hangs on a suspension spring reached from the movement back. Tools: screwdrivers, beat amplifier, oil, and a timing chart.

title: Signature Observatory Lantern Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Observatory Lantern Clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its dial adds a minute ring beside the hour ring, for reading the time to the minute, while keeping the lantern frame and frets.

Mechanism: The minute hand is driven from the centre wheel through the motion work, and the hour hand from the hour wheel, in a weight-driven anchor movement with a pendulum. The anchor gives the accuracy a minute ring needs.

Maintenance: Read the minute ring first and the hour ring second, and set the clock from the minute hand. Wind on schedule and keep the clock level.

Build and restoration: The dial layers separate for cleaning. Tools: screwdrivers, hand puller, oil, and a timing reference.

title: Signature Brass-Fret Lantern Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Brass-Fret Lantern Clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its frets are pierced with a Signature pattern of interlocking rings, cut by hand, and the pattern is repeated on the finial.

Mechanism: The movement is a weight-driven verge and foliot design with a countwheel strike, mounted in the fretted frame. The frets let the bell sound out and let the movement be seen from the sides.

Maintenance: Dust the frets with a soft brush, never a cloth that snags in the piercing. Keep the pillars tight and the clock level.

Build and restoration: Fret repair uses matching brass and soft solder, following the ring pattern. Tools: soft brush, screwdrivers, soft solder, and magnification.

title: Signature Chamber Lantern Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Chamber Lantern Clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. It is a smaller lantern form, 24 centimetres tall, with a carrying handle, made to stand in a bedroom.

Mechanism: A weight-driven verge and pendulum movement keeps time, with a countwheel strike on a small bell. The handle is bolted through the top plate so the clock can be carried safely.

Maintenance: Check the handle before carrying, wind on schedule, and keep the clock level on its stand. Dust the brass with a soft dry cloth.

Build and restoration: The handle bolts are tightened from inside the top plate. Tools: screwdrivers, soft brush, oil, and tweezers.

title: Signature Grand Strike Lantern Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Grand Strike Lantern Clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. It strikes the hour, the half hour, and the quarters on two bells, the most elaborate striking in the Signature lantern range.

Mechanism: A quarter train sounds a blow on the smaller bell at each quarter, and the hour strike follows on the larger bell at the hour. The going train is a weight-driven anchor movement with a pendulum.

Maintenance: Wind all trains on schedule, since the strike trains do heavy work. Keep the bells dust-free and the hammers falling squarely.

Build and restoration: The strike trains are laid out side by side for servicing. Tools: hammer-setting gauge, screwdrivers, oil, and a strike test chart.

title: Signature Calendar Lantern Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Calendar Lantern Clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its dial adds a date aperture driven from the motion work, showing the day of the month beside the hour ring.

Mechanism: The date wheel has 31 teeth and is stepped once per day by a finger on the hour wheel. The going train is a weight-driven anchor movement with a pendulum, and the strike is countwheel-controlled.

Maintenance: Correct the date in the morning, never between 9 at night and 3 in the morning when the finger is engaged. Wind on schedule and keep the clock level.

Build and restoration: The date wheel is reached from the dial back and steps by hand for testing. Tools: tweezers, oil, screwdrivers, and a calendar chart.

title: Signature Night-Watch Lantern Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Night-Watch Lantern Clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its dial numerals are painted large and bold for reading by lamplight, and its strike is a deep single bell that carries through a house.

Mechanism: The movement is a weight-driven verge and foliot design with a countwheel strike on a large bell. The bold numerals are engraved and filled with dark wax for contrast.

Maintenance: Read the clock by the bold hour numeral, and set it by moving the hand to the correct hour. Wind daily and keep the clock level.

Build and restoration: The dial is cleaned with a soft dry brush only, to protect the wax in the engraving. Tools: soft brush, black wax, screwdrivers, and oil.

title: Signature Restorer's Lantern Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Restorer's Lantern Clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its plates are drilled for both foliot and pendulum regulation, so a restorer can study both systems in one frame, and a manual is fixed inside the case.

Mechanism: The movement can be fitted with a foliot or with a pendulum crutch, using the same plates and crown wheel, and the strike is countwheel-controlled in both forms. The manual explains both fittings and their beat rates.

Maintenance: Follow the manual's service interval and record each fitting change on the card inside the case. Wind on schedule and keep the clock level in either form.

Build and restoration: The manual lists every wheel's tooth count and every pivot's size. Tools: screwdrivers, tweezers, oil, bushing tools, and the case manual.

title: Signature Workshop Lantern Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Workshop Lantern Clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its frame is left unpolished and its plates are marked with layout lines, so apprentices can see how a lantern movement is laid out.

Mechanism: The movement is a weight-driven verge and foliot design with a countwheel strike, built to the standard lantern layout with the trains visible from all sides. The layout lines show the depthing of each wheel pair.

Maintenance: Use the clock as a teaching piece: wind it, time it, and compare its beat with a pendulum clock beside it. Keep it level and dust the frame with a soft brush.

Build and restoration: The plates remove on screws for classroom stripping and reassembly. Tools: screwdrivers, depthing tool, oil, tweezers, and a timing chart.

title: Signature Exhibition Lantern Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Exhibition Lantern Clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. It is the largest Signature lantern design, with a glazed display stand, a visible foliot and pendulum pair, and a bell tower top.

Mechanism: Two regulation systems are shown side by side: a foliot on one side and a pendulum on the other, both driven from one weight barrel through separate trains, so visitors can compare their beats. The strike is countwheel-controlled on a large bell.

Maintenance: Wind the clock daily, keep it level on its stand, and keep the glazed stand clean with a dry microfibre cloth. Do not let visitors touch the foliot or pendulum.

Build and restoration: The display stand lifts off for servicing. Tools: microfibre cloth, screwdrivers, oil, tweezers, and a timing chart.
